questions.question: How many censuses had been completed in India as of year 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **15** censuses had been completed in India as of the year 2011.
 
• The census in India is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, but the first complete census was taken in 1881.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country.
 
• The census provides critical data on population demographics, economic activity, literacy and education, housing and household amenities, urbanization, fertility and mortality, and many other socio-economic characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Census** is one of the most reliable sources of data on various demographic and socio-economic parameters.
 
• It helps in planning and formulation of policies for the government at all levels.
 
• The Census of India 2011 was conducted in two phases: the House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010) and the Population Enumeration (9th to 28th February 2011).
 
• India's census is the largest administrative exercise in the world, covering all individuals residing in the country.
 
• The next census was scheduled for 2021 but was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

questions.question: What was India’s population growth rate (in percentage) during 2001-2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __17.64%__

__
 
• **India's population growth rate** during the period **2001-2011** was 17.64%.
 
• This growth rate is calculated based on the census data collected in 2001 and 2011, showing the percentage increase in the population over the decade.
 
• The census is conducted every ten years by the** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner** under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• Population growth rates are crucial for planning and development policies, as they impact resources, infrastructure, and services.
 
• The growth rate reflects various factors including birth rates, death rates, and migration patterns during the decade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **census data** provides comprehensive information on demographic, social, and economic parameters.
 
• The **population growth rate** is a key indicator of demographic trends and is used for various analytical purposes including economic forecasting and infrastructure development.
 
• India's total population as per the 2011 census was approximately **1.21 billion**.
 
• The **decadal growth rate** witnessed a decline from the previous decade (1991-2001), indicating a slowdown in the population increase.
 
• Understanding population dynamics is essential for the effective implementation of government schemes and initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life for citizens.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following states is the most urbanised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa.**__

__
 
• Among the given options, Goa is the most urbanized state, with about **62.2%** of its population living in urban areas (Census 2011).
 
• Tamil Nadu had the highest urbanization rate among large states at **48.4%**, followed by Maharashtra and Gujarat.
 
• Notably, Kerala had a rapid increase in urbanization between 2001 and 2011, with **47.7%** of its population urbanized, primarily due to the reclassification of rural areas.
 
• Punjab had **37.5%** urbanization, while Himachal Pradesh remained one of the least urbanized states with just **10%** of its population living in urban areas.

• **Kerala & Goa:** Both states have seen further increases in urbanization due to development and tourism.
 
• The first full census in India was conducted in **1881** under British rule.
 
• In the **1881** Census of India, the **Madras Presidency** (now part of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala) was among the most urbanized regions.
 
• The first regular census in India was conducted in **1872** by British administrator **W.C. Plowden**. However, it was not synchronous across the entire country and is considered a **partial census.**
 
• **Mumbai** remains one of the most urbanized cities in India, with a population of over **20 million** (2023 estimates).

questions.question: What percentage of the Indian population was estimated to be living below the poverty line in 2011-12?
